desc: Read input values $N, X, Y$ and strings $S, T$.
Decompose both $S$ and $T$ into a list of alternating blocks (e.g., `[(char, length), ...]`).
Check if the number of blocks in $S$ and $T$ are identical; if not, output "No".
Verify that the sequence of characters in the blocks matches between $S$ and $T$ (e.g., if $S$ starts with 0s, $T$ must also start with 0s).

Calculate the required shift for each block to transform $S$ into $T$ and determine if a single consistent shift (or a valid sequence of shifts) can achieve the transformation without violating boundary conditions ($1 \le i \le N-(X+Y)+1$) or block size constraints.
If all conditions are met, output "Yes"; otherwise, output "No".
Implement the code with the corrected logic and local pattern checks.
Write the final Python code implementing the prefix sum difference array logic.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
